sentiment.rationale: Management raised Q3 guidance with high-teens gross bookings growth and low-to-mid-30s EBITDA growth, and announced a $20 billion buyback, signaling strong forward momentum. The Q2 results set all-time highs in audience, frequency, trips, gross bookings, adjusted EBITDA, GAAP operating income, and free cash flow. The tone is confident and forward-looking, with no material risks or cautious language, supporting a moderately bullish score.

summary.revenue: Gross bookings up 18% year-over-year; trips up 18%.
summary.guidance: Q3: high-teens gross bookings growth and low-to-mid-30s EBITDA growth.
key_opportunities: Cross-platform strategy: fewer than 1 in 5 consumers active across both Mobility and Delivery, with cross-platform users having 35% higher retention, 3x gross bookings and profits.
Autonomous vehicle partnerships: expanded with Waymo, WeRide, Baidu, Lucid, Nuro, Wayve, and others; AV utilization in Austin and Atlanta is high.
Lower-cost products (Moto, premium, reserve) driving audience growth; Moto over $1.5B gross bookings growing 40%, premium over $10B growing 35%, reserve growing 60%.
Uber One membership at 36 million, growing 60%, with new surge savings product for Mobility.
Externalizing tech capabilities: advertising business, data collection for AV, Uber AI solutions for data labeling and translation.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Dara Khosrowshahi stated 'We're expecting more of the same strong performance in Q3' and 'we've never been more excited about what Uber is delivering today or the many opportunities ahead.'

evidence.claim: Gross bookings and trips both up 18% year-over-year.
evidence.quote: This powered robust growth in trips and gross bookings, both up 18%.

evidence.claim: Q3 guidance: high-teens gross bookings growth and low-to-mid-30s EBITDA growth.
evidence.quote: We're expecting more of the same strong performance in Q3 with another quarter of high teens gross bookings growth and low to mid-30s EBITDA growth.

evidence.claim: New $20 billion share repurchase authorization announced.
evidence.quote: That's why today, we announced a new $20 billion share repurchase authorization as part of our sustained focus on value creation for our shareholders.

evidence.claim: Cross-platform users have 35% higher retention and generate 3x gross bookings and profits.
evidence.quote: those who kind of use both sides, both mobility and delivery, their retention rates are higher, they are 35% higher than single-business consumers. They generate 3 times the gross bookings and profits than single-business consumers as well.

evidence.claim: Uber One membership at 36 million, growing 60%.
evidence.quote: Uber One 36 million members, and these members spend 3 times more.

evidence.claim: Moto gross bookings over $1.5B growing 40%, premium over $10B growing 35%, reserve growing 60%.
evidence.quote: Moto, which are two-wheelers... it is over kind of $1.5 billion in gross bookings, growing 40%. ...our premium business is now over $10 billion, growing 35% and our reserve business continues to grow 60%.
We're expecting more of the same strong performance in Q3 with another quarter of high teens gross bookings growth and low to mid-30s EBITDA growth.

evidence.claim: AV utilization in Austin and Atlanta is high; average Waymo busier than 99% of drivers.
evidence.quote: the average Waymo is busier than 99% of our drivers in terms of completed trips per day.

evidence.claim: Fewer than 1 in 5 consumers are active across both Mobility and Delivery.
evidence.quote: Today, fewer than 1 in 5 of our consumers are active across both Mobility and Delivery, and we believe this can and will go much higher over time.
